review_notes: I read the whole file. Its only simp-relevant declaration is `comma_iff`, which is `@[simp]` and proved by `Iff.rfl`. It rewrites `comma F₁ F₂ P₁ P₂ X` to `P₁ X.left ∧ P₂ X.right`. That direction is sound. The right-hand side uses the `.left`/`.right` projections, so the definition is not unfolded in a way that could loop or compete with other rules. I found no other simp lemma that could overlap with it. `ObjectProperty.prop_inverseImage_iff` in Basic.lean is the closest candidate, but it applies to `inverseImage`, not to `comma`. The `variable {F₁ F₂} in` line makes `F₁ F₂` implicit, so simp can infer them from `X`. The two uses I found are `simp only [comma_iff] at hf` in this file and `ObjectProperty.comma` in Presentable/Comma.lean:162. The Presentable file unfolds with `prop_inverseImage_iff`, not `comma_iff`. That is a minor stylistic difference and not a defect in this file's simp interface. I did not check every downstream use in the repository. Lean was not run.
